title: International Cooperation: Ideals, Instruments, and Evidence
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 四つの原文段落と全九つの学習対象を保持し、元の日本語記述問題を根拠のある英語四択へ変換しました。

passages.text:
After the Second World War, governments created an international organization for cooperation in education, science, culture, and communication. Its constitution begins from an ambitious idea: lasting peace cannot rest only on political and economic agreements; it also requires intellectual and moral solidarity. This is a mission statement, not evidence that educational exchange automatically prevents conflict.

The organization works through several instruments. Member states negotiate conventions, declarations, and recommendations. Experts develop shared terminology, data, ethical guidance, and scientific programs. Networks connect schools, universities, archives, laboratories, and protected sites. These activities can lower the cost of cooperation: participants do not need to invent new standards and contacts for every project.

Yet designation is not implementation. Placing a site on an international list does not transfer ownership to the organization, guarantee funding, or physically protect it from war, neglect, tourism pressure, or climate hazards. A convention creates obligations only through legal and administrative systems that states build and enforce. International monitoring may supply information and public attention, but attention is a mechanism, not the final outcome.

Evaluation should therefore use intermediate questions. Did a program create comparable data? Did it preserve records, train specialists, change a curriculum, or help states coordinate? Were local communities included, and who defined the value being protected? The institution's ideals matter because they organize action, but ideals gain credibility only when procedures are transparent, affected people can participate, and results are independently examined.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Educational exchange automatically eliminates armed conflict.

options.label: B
options.text: International cooperation should be assessed through its instruments, implementation, participation, and evidence rather than its ideals alone.

options.label: C
options.text: International designation transfers ownership and funding of every protected site.

options.label: D
options.text: Mission statements provide sufficient proof that an institution is effective.

questions.answer: 正解：B。The passage connects ideals with instruments, implementation, participation, and independently examined results. instrument は「制度的手段」、implementation は「実施」です。A・C・Dは本文が明確に退ける自動的効果です。

questions.prompt: Why does paragraph 1 distinguish a mission statement from evidence?

options.label: A
options.text: A statement identifies goals and values, but causal effectiveness must be tested through activities, implementation, and results.

options.label: B
options.text: A mission statement has no influence on how an institution organizes action.

options.label: C
options.text: A constitution automatically proves that educational exchange prevents every conflict.

options.label: D
options.text: Evidence is needed only when an institution lacks political agreements.

questions.answer: 正解：A。A mission statement shows the intended purpose, but it does not establish a causal effect. causal effectiveness は「因果的な有効性」で、実際の活動・履行・比較可能な結果による検証が必要です。

questions.prompt: The phrase “lower the cost of cooperation” in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to

options.label: A
options.text: make shared work easier by providing standards, data, and networks

options.label: B
options.text: remove every political disagreement among member states

options.label: C
options.text: guarantee enough money for every international project

options.label: D
options.text: replace national institutions with one international authority

questions.answer: 正解：A。Here, cost includes time, uncertainty, and the effort of creating contacts and standards—not only money. 共通語彙・データ・ネットワークが調整負担を軽くするという意味です。

questions.prompt: Which option identifies three kinds of institutional instruments described in paragraph 2?

options.label: A
options.text: Military alliances, private ownership transfers, and compulsory tourism

options.label: B
options.text: Automatic funding, physical barriers, and national character

options.label: C
options.text: Agreements and recommendations, shared expert guidance and programs, and networks linking institutions

options.label: D
options.text: Election campaigns, trade tariffs, and criminal courts

questions.answer: 正解：C。The passage names conventions, declarations, recommendations; shared terminology, data, ethics, and scientific programs; and institutional networks. convention は「国家間の条約」、recommendation は「勧告」です。

questions.prompt: Why does placement on an international list not guarantee preservation?

options.label: A
options.text: Listing prevents international monitoring from collecting information.

options.label: B
options.text: Ownership, funding, enforcement, and local hazards remain separate practical matters that designation alone cannot resolve.

options.label: C
options.text: Every listed site is immediately transferred to the international organization.

options.label: D
options.text: Climate hazards affect only sites that are not internationally recognized.

questions.answer: 正解：B。Designation（指定・登録）は ownership, funding, enforcement, or physical protection を自動的に与えません。戦争、放置、観光圧力、気候災害への現地対応が別に必要です。

questions.prompt: Why are national legal and administrative systems still necessary after a convention is adopted?

options.label: A
options.text: They allow states to ignore every obligation created by the agreement.

options.label: B
options.text: They determine which sites the international organization will own directly.

options.label: C
options.text: They translate international obligations into budgets, permits, education, enforcement, and daily management.

options.label: D
options.text: They prove that public attention is the same as a final outcome.

questions.answer: 正解：C。A convention creates obligations, but domestic institutions must turn them into routine action. obligation は「履行すべき義務」であり、予算・許認可・教育・保存管理・執行が必要です。

questions.prompt: What is one advantage of evaluating intermediate outcomes rather than asking only whether war was prevented?

options.label: A
options.text: Intermediate outcomes make local participation unnecessary.

options.label: B
options.text: They prove that peace has only one cause.

options.label: C
options.text: They remove the need to examine procedures independently.

options.label: D
options.text: Results such as comparable data, preserved records, and trained specialists provide a more testable path from activity to outcome.

questions.answer: 正解：D。Peace has many causes and a difficult counterfactual（反実仮想）, whereas intermediate results can be connected more directly to a program. intermediate は「最終結果へ至る途中の」です。

questions.prompt: What does the sentence “Attention is a mechanism, not the final outcome” imply?

options.label: A
options.text: Public attention may encourage monitoring, funding, or pressure, but it does not itself guarantee preservation or fair participation.

options.label: B
options.text: Monitoring has no possible effect on institutional behavior.

options.label: C
options.text: International attention automatically protects a site from every hazard.

options.label: D
options.text: Publicity is the only valid measure of cultural cooperation.

questions.answer: 正解：A。Attention can activate other processes, so it is a mechanism（作用の仕組み）rather than preservation itself. 注目は監視・資金・政治的圧力を促し得ますが、保存や公正な参加を保証しません。

questions.prompt: Which evaluation plan best follows the passage's approach to measuring a heritage-cooperation program?

options.label: A
options.text: Count media mentions and assume that greater visibility proves permanent preservation.

options.label: B
options.text: Track legal protection, funding, trained staff, and site condition; consult local residents; compare similar sites; and examine durability and distributional costs.

options.label: C
options.text: Use the institution's mission statement as the only evidence of success.

options.label: D
options.text: Measure tourist numbers while excluding residents from decisions about protected value.

questions.answer: 正解：B。This plan tests implementation, physical results, participation, comparison, durability, and costs. durability は「長期的に持続する性質」、distributional costs は「負担が誰に配分されるか」です。
